0.original: Wuk Lamat thinks it time to gather her allies for the road ahead.

29.original: Wait at the designated location again.

30.original: Wait at the designated location once more.

48.original: I still haven't had one bite of Namikka's food thanks to Papa's nonsense, so I'm going back to finish my plate before I head out.

49.original: I've otherwise asked everyone to meet at the For'ard Cabins. Come and join us after you've had a moment to recover, eh?

51.original: Await your companions and continue with the rite of succession?

54.original: Is that it? You're all set to go?

55.original: I left Eorzea prepared to travel in search of work, so I had few belongings to begin with. Bidding farewell to my fellow artisans took rather a lot of time, however.

56.original: Again, I appreciate you making this commitment, Fonjeantaine.

57.original: Shall we depart for Earthenshire, then?

59.original: Wuk Evu, what are you doing here?

60.original: Ahhh! I spend my days correcting manners, and here I am perpetrating the grave offense of delaying the Third Promise's departure!

61.original: Please, take up your axe and rend my flesh unto taco meat!

62.original: Must your demands be so gruesome!? Besides, I told you that kind of thing doesn't bother me!

63.original: All right, then. I won't let it bother me either.

65.original: I'd come to the city to purchase supplies when I spotted your entourage getting ready to leave. You seek the city of gold, if I'm not mistaken?

66.original: That's right─it's the final step of the rite of succession. If you know anything about the subject, I'd love to hear it.

67.original: Then allow me to be of service. As you know, legends of the golden city have been passed down in Tural for a thousand years.

68.original: Yet when it comes to describing the place itself, the stories do not always agree. Some portray it as one might expect: a glittering metropolis of golden towers. Others suggest it is more unassuming and owes the name to a fabulous treasure hidden at its heart.

69.original: Every telling, however, has a common thread: those who go in search of the golden city do not return.

70.original: The lesson to be learned from this, Third Promise, is that to seek the legend is to court death. I must implore you to proceed with the utmost care.

71.original: That is all I wished to say. I shall pray for your safe journey.

73.original: What are we to make of these cautionary tales? If every expedition has ended in tragedy, how then did the Dawnservant find the city and return without incident?

74.original: It seems the legend originated with the Yok Huy. Speaking with them remains our strongest lead, I feel.

75.original: A lead we shall follow in time. But first, let us see Fonjeantaine safely into the Moblins' care.

76.original: We're back, and we've brought with us a willing potsworn. This is Fonjeantaine, a talented goldsmith who once worked at Eshtaime's Aesthetics in Ul'dah.

77.original: Wonderful! Impressive! You are first to return, Third Promise!

78.original: And with an artisan from across the salt, no less! We welcome you and your unique skills to Earthenshire. Helphand will show you to the Workpot.

79.original: This is it, then. I look forward to hearing you proclaimed Dawnservant!

80.original: Thank you, Fonjeantaine. I'll be sure not to disappoint you.

81.original: You have reachmet the requirements of the Feat of Pots. Rediroq presents your keystone with joysmiles and wellwishing!

83.original: Pfff... Pfffkohhh... More potsworn candidates!? Come, come, tell Rediroq your tales!

84.original: Another feat accomplished, another keystone acquired.

85.original: Ohohoho, you <hex:021A020203>are<hex:021A020103> doing well. I expected nothing less of Zoraal Ja's esteemed siblings.

86.original: Your cleverness in particular is most admirable, Second Promise. We must have you apply that Sharlayan knowledge you so cherish, and arm Tural with weapons of magitek design.

87.original: ...In your role as the new Dawnservant's chief advisor, of course.

88.original: The tools of war hold no interest for me. I wish only to improve our nation through practical innovations.

89.original: Foreign powers will think twice about testing our strength once Tuliyollal is known for its advanced technology.

90.original: Just as the Garlean Empire was deterred from invading Sharlayan.

91.original: That may well be true... But how long will it take Tuliyollal to progress to this advanced state? How many years?

92.original: With a collective commitment to education and hard work, it should not take so very─

94.original: Easier to expand our territory...and swallow Sharlayan whole.

95.original: Conquer other nations through force of arms, and you're looking at a future of uprisings and bloodshed. Yours wouldn't be the first failed empire.

96.original: Then we keep fighting, until the mounting costs convince them to lay down their weapons. Until all have grown tired of loss.

97.original: How would such an outcome bring anyone joy!? What you propose is a mockery of peace!

98.original: Pfff... Pfffkohhh... Rediroq is reminded of days long ago.

99.original: In the time before Tuliyollal, there were no potpacts for the potsworn. It was normal to grabsnatch artisans, and force them to work for Mobbies.

100.original: Until the day Gulool Ja Ja arrived. The families of the grabsnatched pleaded with him, and so he came to Earthenshire.

101.original: Mobbies are not a warmake people. We feared death had come for us, but Gulool Ja Ja just wanted to talk!

102.original: (-Vow of Reason Gulool Ja Ja-)Be at ease. We are here to trade words, not blows.

103.original: (-Vow of Reason Gulool Ja Ja-)The goldwork crafted in this village is superb. One can tell at a glance the quality of materials used; the mastery of technique employed.

104.original: (-Vow of Reason Gulool Ja Ja-)Yet it does not stir the heart. A goblet shaped by bound hands and broken spirit is devoid of luster.

105.original: (-Vow of Reason Gulool Ja Ja-)Compare that now to the works of a joyful artisan. She pours her very soul into her creations, and they shine like the newly risen sun. Have you not seen this to be true?

106.original: And so began the custom of goodliving. Happy potsworn make good works, and good works make Mobbies happy!

107.original: Gulool Ja Ja's words were wise! Joysmiles did indeed bring fine craft and much jinglyshine!

108.original: So the Head of Reason was behind the forging of potpacts...

109.original: Yes! Reason and cleverthink changed Mobbies' way of life!

111.original: The First Promise tires of your talk of olden days. He would rather look to the future, and the next feat.

112.original: We should be getting on as well.

113.original: Bakool Ja Ja never did come back, did he?

114.original: Pfff... Pfffkohhh... Do you have a moment, Third Promise?

115.original: Rakorok would repay you for handhelping with Kaahe. He brings a tale of the golden city!

116.original: Really? I'd love to hear it!

117.original: The towers, the streets, all fashioned from gold. Everywhere you look, every splendor you can imagine!

118.original: The young, the old, and everyone in between, they live in golden happiness. A city of eternal bliss, forever perched above the clouds!

119.original: Everything fashioned from gold, eh? And just imagine everyone living in golden happiness─now that's a city I'd like to visit!

120.original: Excuse me, Rakorok, where did you hear that particular tale?

121.original: From our longtime Yok Huy friends! They live up in the mountains, in Urqopacha.

123.original: Seems everything is pointing us their way!

124.original: This feat and everything leading up to it has taught me much about the Moblin way of life. I'll be sad to leave Earthenshire and your joysmiles behind!

125.original: These tales raise many questions... Let us hope the giants have answers.

126.original: The stories describe a place of boundless happiness, but are also rife with dire warnings of seekers who did not return. What are we to make of this...?

127.original: It unsettles me that Zoraal Ja is even a claimant in the first place. Surely his father cannot condone his violent ambitions...

128.original: The Head of Reason in Rediroq's story sounds so different from the Head of Resolve. They share the same body, yet their personalities are wholly distinct.

129.original: Worry not for potsworn Fonjeantaine! He is in good helphands!

130.original: Right, we should go and see the giants next!

131.original: Agreed. Golden mysteries notwithstanding, their village is featured prominently in the saga and is not to be ignored.

132.original: The Urqopacha highlands should be easy enough to reach from here.

133.original: If we leave Earthenshire from the west, there's a road which leads up into the mountains. Let's find that first.

134.original: This road will take us through the mountains to the Urqopacha highlands. An exhausting route, perhaps, but a straightforward one.

135.original: We're to meet with the Yok Huy at last...

136.original: The highlands are where the Lay of Proof took place─that being Gulool Ja Ja's encounter with the Yok Huy.

137.original: But 'tis also the stage for the Lay of Ice, where heroes fought the monstrous Valigarmanda. I am most curious to know what the rite will demand of us there...

138.original: One day we're sailing up rivers, and the next we're hiking up mountains.

139.original: Looks like the trail is going to get steep from here on in. I hope everyone is ready for some climbing!

141.original: (-Bright-haired Tonawawtan Man-)I'm glad I caught you... Rediroq asked me to bring you back to the village.

142.original: (-Bright-haired Tonawawtan Man-)She says there's something she forgot to give you.

143.original: Huh...? Something other than the keystone?

144.original: (-Bright-haired Tonawawtan Man-)Yes, an item of great importance, or so I was told. It shouldn't take long, if you would please follow me.

145.original: I wonder what this is all about? Well, no need for everyone to come─I'll be back in a little while!

146.original: Pfff... Pfffkohhh... Moblins are busy ensuring goodliving for new potsworn! Rediroq has no time for idle tongueflaps!

147.original: He had rather interesting hair for a Hyur...or should I say Tonawawta? In any case, strange that I never noticed him while we were in Earthenshire.

148.original: Knowing Wuk Lamat, she was probably eating sweets behind our backs and forgot to pay the shopkeeper or something equally careless.

149.original: I'm eager to continue to the highlands and meet a Yok Huy face-to-face. We've heard much about them, but I'm not entirely sure what to expect.

150.original: That man seemed familiar somehow... But I just can't place him.

151.original: This is taking quite a while... Just keep waiting for now, I suppose.

152.original: Perhaps there were complications? Well, let us wait a little longer.

153.original: This is getting a little ridiculous. Did she get lost on the way back to find us?

154.original: But how? There's only the one road.

155.original: I wouldn't underestimate Wuk Lamat's sense of direction...or lack thereof.

156.original: Fortunately, she has a linkpearl. Let's see what's keeping her, shall we?

157.original: She's not responding... Perhaps we should all return to Earthenshire.

158.original: 'Twas Rediroq who had business with her, yes?

159.original: She doesn't seem to be here...

160.original: I'd thought Wuk Lamat was just being her usual impulsive self, but now I'm not so certain...

161.original: I pray naught untoward has befallen the Third Promise.

162.original: Something's not right. I can feel it...

163.original: Pfff... Pfffkohhh... Back again so soon?

164.original: We've come looking for Wuk Lamat. Did you not send someone to fetch her?

165.original: Rediroq did not! Neither has she seen the Third Promise since you were last here.

166.original: Then who was that man who came for her...?

167.original: Oh? I thought you'd left already.

168.original: Where is Lamaty'i? Is she not with you?

169.original: You don't <hex:021A020203>know<hex:021A020103> where she is? How could you let this happen!?

170.original: That thou shouldst worry for thy sister is understandable. Yet rather than assign blame, thine energies are better spent on locating her.

171.original: I will help you search. This is not how I'd wish a fellow claimant to lose the contest─my sister least of all.

172.original: In that case, dividing our forces will allow us to cover more ground.

173.original: <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203> and I should work together at least, the better to facilitate communication between our groups.

174.original: Then the rest of us will split up. Report in should you find anything.

175.original: We'll be on our way as well.
